name: Huffman Coding
description: A greedy algorithm that builds an optimal prefix-free binary code for a set of characters based on their frequencies. A min-priority queue (min-heap) stores nodes sorted by frequency. At each step, the two nodes with the lowest frequencies are extracted, combined into a new internal node whose frequency is their sum, and reinserted into the queue. This process repeats until a single tree remains. Characters with higher frequencies receive shorter bit codes (closer to the root), minimizing the total encoded length.

testCases.name: Classic textbook example
testCases.description: The classic CLRS example: 'a' (highest frequency) gets a 1-bit code, while 'f' and 'e' (lowest frequencies) get the longest codes, demonstrating optimal prefix-free encoding

testCases.name: Equal frequencies
testCases.description: When all characters have equal frequency, the resulting Huffman tree is a balanced binary tree where all codes have the same length (2 bits for 4 characters)

testCases.name: Skewed frequency distribution
testCases.description: Highly skewed frequencies produce a very unbalanced tree: 'p' gets a 1-bit code while rare characters get longer codes, maximizing compression for the common case
